title: 'I can't believe I did it': TikToker completes 60km run across all 32 East-West Line MRT stations in a day
text:

 lifestyle 'I can't believe I did it': TikToker completes 60km run across all 32 East-West Line MRT stations in a day
 With no prior training or preparation, Xander pushed through leg cramps, exhaustion and the scorching midday sun to complete his challenge. A TikToker took on a 60km challenge to run the entire MRT East-West Line, covering all 32 stations. PHOTO: Screengrab/TikTok/Xanderys PUBLISHED ON November 18, 2026 9:00 AM BY Crystal Tan While most people would take the train to travel across Singapore, one man decided to make the journey on foot.
 A TikToker, Xander, challenged himself to run the entire MRT East-West Line, successfully completing a 60km journey covering 32 stations in one day.
 Xander started his journey at Tuas Link MRT station, making his way across Singapore before eventually reaching his final destination at Changi Airport MRT station. 
 The video began with a question: "Is it possible to run the entire East-West Line in one day?" alongside an image of the MRT map.
 To make it more challenging, he claimed he was attempting the feat with "no training, no preparation, and no sleep".
 He then set off on his challenge, admitting that he was unsure of what to expect.
 "I've never ran more than 21km before and I'm honestly just worried about how my body is gonna react to that crazy volume," he said in the video.
 Battling leg cramps, scorching heat
 As the sun came out, Xander shared he was forced to slow down and walk after experiencing leg cramps.
 "After six hours running, I completely hit the wall," he admitted.
 By that point, he had already covered approximately a marathon's distance but still had another half-marathon to go.
 Despite the exhaustion and scorching midday heat, he pressed on, eventually reaching the final stretch of his journey.
 He said in the video: "Even though it got super hot at noon, I just kept going and before I knew it, we finally reached Expo station."
 He described the last 8km leading to his final station, Changi Airport, as the most difficult, having to endure the scorching sun throughout.
 Reflecting on how far he had come, he said he was amazed that the journey had started on the other side of Singapore.
 "Holy s***. Holy s***, we did it," he said upon reaching the final station and completing the challenge.
 "32 out of 32 stations on the East-West Line. 60km all by foot. I can't believe I did it man."
 Xander ended the video with an encouraging message: "It goes to show you can do anything. As long as you don't stop, you will never fail."
 AsiaOne has contacted Xander for more information.
